text:
Alex P: I'm heading offline in ~15m, handing primary to Maria. Leaving context for the ongoing routing-service memory growth incident.

Alex P: Summary: routing-service in us-east-1 has slow memory growth causing periodic worker OOMs and evictions. Impact: increased 5xxs for short-running text-generation routes and elevated latency spikes for ~10% of requests. Pager noise started ~2h ago.

Alex P: Active alerts:
- routing-service.mem_rss > 80% for nodepool-prod (alert id: RS-MEM-742)
- worker-restarts count spike (alert id: RS-RESTART-91)
- customer-latency-slo breach for route /v1/generate (alert id: SLO-GEN-12)

Alex P: Mitigations in progress (do not restart primary autoscaler unless told):
1) Samir reduced batch_size from 128->64 on canary pool to reduce memory pressure (deployed at 2163509200).
2) Priya enabled prefix-KV cache bypass for low-priority requests (to drop memory usage per session).
3) We're draining one of the suspect worker pods and replacing it with a CPU-fallback service (cpu-fallback:v2) to reduce GPU mem contention.

Alex P: Current runbook pointers: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/routing-memory-leak (section 3.2 live mitigation). Also see /runbooks/ooms in Ops Playbooks.

Maria L: taking primary. Thanks Alex. Quick Q: which customers are currently experiencing errors?

Alex P: top affected customers (based on error-rate and support flags):
- UnitaryDocs (support P1) - sporadic 502s during long prompts
- VectorSuite - higher tail latency, minor errors
- internal-bench - test traffic has amplified the issue after a long prompt load

Samir R: note: we've throttled test-client tokens from internal-bench at the LB level. That dropped error spikes by ~30% at 2163509300.

Maria L: ok. Immediate plan from me:
- keep canary at reduced batch size, monitor mem_rss and restart-rate for 30m
- if mem_rss remains >85% for canary, roll back canary to cpu-fallback for the rest of the pool and promote autoscaling profile fallback (autoscale-profile:mem-conservative).
- notify SRE and Support for potential customer-impact communications

Priya K: FYI I've left a sticky note in the runbook: `if you replace worker images, use image tag sha:a7c3 (contains leak mitigation patch)` - don't use latest, it's unverified.

incident-bot: Alert RS-MEM-742 acknowledged by Alex P at 2163509255.

pagerduty: Pager duty note: on-call escalation locked to Maria L as primary, Samir R as secondary.

Maria L: I'll take ownership of the page routing and follow the runbook. Samir, can you keep an eye on LB throttles and customer backoffs? Priya, stay on patch verification.

Samir R: on it. I'll also spin up a small extra worker in a different AZ (us-east-1b) with the mem-conservative profile to absorb traffic if needed.

Alex P: handoff checklist:
- primary transferred to Maria (done)
- secondary is Samir (notified)
- active mitigations documented above (do not revert batch_size change unless CPU spike >85%)
- support notified of top impacted customers and drafting a status blurb if errors persist (>15m continued).

Maria L: noted. If anyone needs to escalate to on-call lead, ping me and then @oncall-leads. I'll open a short bridge if errors reappear after any config change.

Priya K: I'll run the mem-diff script on the drained pod dump and upload to the incident channel: `/ops/tools/mem-diff --pod routing-suspect-3 > /tmp/memdump.2163509400.log`

Alex P: thanks all. Leaving now, reachable by DM for 20m. Good handoff. :thumbsup:

Maria L: thanks Alex — taking primary, will update this thread with status every 15m or on any escalation.

Samir R: logging first checkpoint: canary mem_rss now 62% after batch change, restart-rate down to baseline. Continuing to monitor.

Maria L: recorded next check at ~2163510250. If mem_rss climbs >80% again, we'll plan a controlled image swap to cpu-fallback across the suspect AZ.

Maria L: (added) Support blurb draft: "We're investigating increased errors for some long-prompt requests in us-east-1. Engineering is actively mitigating; some customers may see transient errors or higher latency. We'll post updates in the next 30 minutes."
